Obtained result: a certified family of recurrent reaction-record inferences

I developed two complementary constructions beyond the single-opening interface.

The stronger repeated-inference operation now handles a hidden recurrent controller, genuinely coupled reaction hazards, overlapping reaction interfaces, and repeated conditioning while preserving a fixed number of retained mixture components. Its certificate can cover an entire bounded observation workload before the particular record is known.

A second construction removes the unchanged-silent-generator restriction: when the local killed generators commute, recurrent controller dynamics can be integrated through occupation moments, with a proved bound on the number of positive product operators required.

Both have new executable code and actual retained rational operators. The repeated-inference construction also reused the existing correlated entrance and retained its resulting posterior. The mathematical extensions and executed specializations are distinguished below.

The candidate contribution is now quite specific:

Obtain, from checked compact rules, an executable reaction-query interface together with a representation bound and a conditional-law error bound for a declared family of future observations.

The comparison with established methods concerns that complete obtaining-and-execution contract. Occupation formulas, trajectory conditioning, positive operators, averaging and projective error propagation each have substantial antecedents.

# A source-obtained record interface for a recurrent fast hidden controller

This is new scientific construction. Its executable is `fast_switching_event_kernel.py`; it does not recover any missing historical helpers. The retained scientific objects are `fast_switching_record_interface_24sites.json` and `fast_switching_record_posterior_24sites.json`. Numerical results are in `fast_switching_event_kernel_results.json`.

## 1. The operation and its conditions

The operation is an **unnormalized first-event likelihood operator**, followed when required by conditional state inference. It accepts an arbitrary joint input law of the hidden controller and all leaves. For a requested elapsed time and observed mark, it returns a positive product propagation followed by the exact marked guard/reset map, together with an entrywise relative certificate. The input law is a runtime argument. Neither independence of that law nor stationary initialization of the controller is assumed by the certificate.

Let a symmetric two-state controller \(C_s\in\{-1,+1\}\) switch at rate \(\nu>0\) in each direction. Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) have independent finite silent generators \(Q_i\), unchanged by the controller. Independence here describes the generator, not the initial distribution. Marked reaction rules have nonnegative rates and specified reset maps. Let \(V(c,x)\) be the sum of the rates of **all** marked events, including marks other than the requested one. Before the first marked event, the full generator is the independent silent generator killed at rate \(V\).

Assume the source establishes

\[
\bar V(x)=\frac{V(+1,x)+V(-1,x)}2
       =d_0+\sum_i d_i(x_i),\qquad d_0,d_i\ge0,
\]

and obtains a finite bound

\[
h(x)=\frac{V(+1,x)-V(-1,x)}2,\qquad |h(x)|\le A.
\]

The phasewise hazards may be coupled on a connected graph. Only their stationary average has to be additive. In particular, a local multiplicative hazard is not being mistaken for a separable killed semigroup.

Write \(D_i=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)\), and let \(J_j\) be the complete nonnegative jump/reset matrix for the observed mark \(j\). It includes every source branch with that mark; the branch need not be observed. The proposed compact operator is

\[
\bar K_j(t)=e^{-d_0t}
 \left(P_C(t)\otimes_i e^{(Q_i-D_i)t}\right)J_j.
\tag{1}
\]

# A recurrent-controller event kernel obtained from occupation moments

New Pro3 construction. This is a proved obtaining algorithm with a newly
implemented binary specialization documented in Section 10. It removes the
single-opening requirement and allows the silent local generator to change
with a hidden recurrent controller. The tractable condition is commutation
of the two local killed generators. No global reaction or configuration
expansion is required by the acquisition algorithm.

The output is an unnormalized event-time-density operator with a relative
certificate valid for every supplied initial joint law, including correlated
positive mixtures and nonnegative tensor trains. Ordinary programmes and
existing inference methods may acquire and retain the same operator.

## 1. Source conditions and the scientific operation

Let C_t be an autonomous two-state continuous-time Markov chain with generator

    C=[[-lambda,lambda],[mu,-mu]],       lambda,mu>0.

Its switches leave the local physical states unchanged. Module i has a finite
state space, silent generator Q_i(c), and diagonal nonnegative recorded-event
killing D_i(c) in controller state c. Conditional on a controller path, the
modules evolve independently until the first recorded event. Set

    A_i(c)=Q_i(c)-D_i(c).

The total pre-event killing is additive. The selected final mark/reset
operator J is supplied as a finite positive sum of local tensor factors,
including a factor on the controller when necessary. Its row sums must be
consistent with the event intensities included in the killing. J can retain
or reset the controller and can have finitely many reset branches.

The essential algebraic condition is

    A_i(0) A_i(1)=A_i(1) A_i(0)          for every i.       (1)

For rational local source matrices, (1) is decided by exact local matrix
multiplication. No commutation between generators of different modules is
an additional requirement: their lifted actions already commute.
The finite controller/component decomposition and additive killing must be
supplied or obtained by checked structural analysis of the compact rule
source. Enumerating finite local states is allowed; a compact decomposition
for an arbitrary rule program is not assumed to exist or to be free to find.

Fix an observation lag t>0. The pre-event survival operator P_t retains the
controller endpoint and every local state.
